claims.statement: Poland had 1,631,400 prosumer installations at the end of April 2026 and 127,386 prosumer storage systems at the end of March 2026, creating a large installed base but a much smaller storage-led initial segment.
Official Polish guidance identifies self-consumption and storage management as core net-billing levers and describes hourly-price scheduling, so the optimisation trigger is real.

URE's 2026 approved household tariff averages 495.16 PLN/MWh for the energy component and reports 1.8 MWh average annual G11 consumption, so a 180-420 PLN annual software fee is a demanding household denominator unless flexible-load savings or installer value is directly measured.

SolarEdge already bundles tariff-, weather-, load- and battery-aware optimisation, device scheduling and homeowner control in SolarEdge ONE, making a generic optimiser reproducible and vulnerable to OEM bundling.

OEM data access is technically possible but commercially and operationally gated: SolarEdge documents rate limits, while Fronius restricts productive Solar.web Query API access to contracted business partners and charges by data package.

The EU Data Act supports a user's ability to request readily available connected-product data for a chosen third party, but it does not create a personal-data legal basis, eliminate security or trade-secret controls, or confer remote-control and firmware-alteration rights.

A savings report needs an explicit measurement boundary and baseline method because whole-site bills mix the intervention with weather, occupancy and other changes; the artifact is not defensible merely because an optimisation model is useful.

contrary_evidence: SolarEdge ONE already performs the core tariff-, weather-, load- and battery-aware optimisation and controls devices inside its ecosystem.
Fronius offers a professional API for monitoring, O&M, smart-home and control uses, so an OEM or platform can bundle much of the data layer.

The average G11 household's energy-supply component makes the proposed annual software fee material before distribution, taxes and fixed charges; the addressable value is concentrated in higher-consumption flexible-load homes.
The Data Act improves user-directed data access but does not grant remote-control, firmware or warranty authority and retains GDPR, security and trade-secret constraints.
A protocol library and AI-generated optimiser are reproducible; durable value must come from permissioned integrations, longitudinal interventions and installer adoption of the report.

economics.acquisition_route: Use 30-50 authorised sites from the family company to deliver the single-OEM report against pre-specified baselines, then seek paid report orders from three unrelated installers around live service or retrofit events. Do not count wholesalers, subscriptions or additional OEMs as distribution until the event-priced workflow shows positive installer economics.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Not established by current evidence. The event-priced wedge is a validation mechanism, not yet a wealth-scale model: it must first show repeat paid report volume and positive contribution margin, after which recurring or broader-device expansion would still require new evidence. Do not count hypothetical future SaaS revenue or business value.
economics.founder_time: Three to four hours per day is feasible for one read-only adapter and a bounded report workflow if family-company installers handle customer communication and all equipment changes. Continuous monitoring, additional OEMs and direct homeowner support remain out of scope until staffing and unit economics justify them.
economics.gross_margin_basis: The event model avoids continuous monitoring and multi-vendor support during validation, but bill normalisation, API charges, analyst review and installer support remain variable delivery costs. Measure contribution margin per completed report; do not assume the 70-85% mature software margin until delivery is sufficiently automated.
economics.payback: Accept an installer-paid report only when one avoided diagnostic visit or attributable incremental retrofit gross profit is expected to cover the full report price; test and record that result per event rather than relying on forecast household savings.
economics.pricing: Test 300-700 PLN as a fixed per-report price hypothesis, paid by the installer around a service or retrofit event. Do not offer the 10-25 PLN per-site monthly workflow or a recurring homeowner fee in the initial product.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Repeat revenue comes only from new service and retrofit events at installers that found the prior report economically useful. Renewal is not assumed; track reorder rate and the share of reports tied to avoided visits or incremental retrofits.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: An accumulating, versioned corpus of single-OEM baseline-to-intervention cases can improve report templates, counterfactual estimates and installer trust, but it becomes a durable advantage only if unrelated installers repeatedly buy reports and contribute permissioned outcomes.
fingerprint.customer: Polish residential PV installers that already service a material installed base on one supported inverter family, initially for battery, heat-pump or EV-charging homes with a live service-call or retrofit decision.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Use the family installation company to test the one-OEM report on 30-50 authorised sites, then seek paid orders for the same report from three unrelated installers around live service or retrofit events; do not pursue wholesalers, recurring monitoring or additional OEMs until those paid events show positive installer economics.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A single-OEM, read-only diagnostic and verification report that imports authorised history, applies a pre-specified baseline and quantifies a service or retrofit decision; sold per completed installer event, with recurring monitoring, remote control and additional OEM adapters deferred.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The installer pays once for a completed report when deciding whether to avoid a site visit, make a qualified configuration change or recommend a retrofit; no recurring homeowner or installer subscription is part of the initial product.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A supported-site service call or retrofit inquiry where the installer must decide whether a visit, configuration change, battery, EMS, heat-pump or EV-charging intervention is economically justified.

founder_fit: The family renewable-energy company provides an unusually credible, low-social-cost route to a bounded pilot and access to installer workflows.
Forecasting, counterfactual measurement and tariff simulation fit the founder's data-science strengths.
A read-first product with all physical or control changes executed by qualified installers limits safety exposure and is compatible with continued employment.
The founder must hold the scope to one protocol and installer-facing support; multi-OEM homeowner support would exceed the stated part-time envelope.

redesign.economic_effect: Replacing unvalidated recurring monitoring with a 300-700 PLN fixed-price report ties revenue to an observable service or retrofit event, lets the pilot test whether one avoided visit or incremental retrofit gross profit covers delivery, and postpones continuous support and multi-OEM integration costs; repeat volume, margin and wealth-scale expansion remain unproven.

risks: Poor advice or unapproved control could increase bills, reduce comfort, accelerate battery degradation or create warranty and safety disputes.
OEM API terms, quotas, pricing or account permissions can strand an adapter or eliminate margin.
Savings claims without a documented baseline can create consumer-protection and installer-liability exposure.
OEMs can bundle optimisation and installer dashboards, leaving the product without a scarce control point.
Multi-vendor edge cases and homeowner support can turn a software product into an incompatible part-time services business.

structure.commercial_archetype: Single-OEM, event-priced installer diagnostic and verification workflow
structure.control_point: The paid, versioned baseline and intervention report used for one live service or retrofit decision
structure.critical_dependency: Authorised, sufficiently granular data from one supported inverter family plus evidence that independent installers pay for the report because an avoided visit or incremental retrofit value covers its price

thesis: Start with one supported inverter family and sell Polish installers a read-only, fixed-price diagnostic and verification report only when a live service call or retrofit decision exists. The report uses authorised meter and inverter history and a pre-specified baseline to test whether a visit, qualified setting change or hardware intervention is economically justified; the family-company pilot proves delivery, and three unrelated paid installer trials must prove the event economics before any recurring monitoring, remote control or multi-OEM expansion.
title: Single-OEM Event-Priced PV Diagnostic for Installers
uncertainties: Incremental bill savings over OEM defaults and simple schedules are unknown and require a pre-specified field test.
Installer willingness to pay for recurring monitoring, avoided truck rolls or retrofit qualification is unknown.
Account-level API permission, commercial reuse rights, control rights and warranty treatment differ by OEM and remain unknown beyond the documented examples.
The number of Polish sites combining batteries or other controllable high loads with supported devices and installers willing to participate is unknown.
Wholesaler, buying-group and installer referral channels are hypotheses with no commitment evidence.
The 20000-site wealth scenario, contribution margin and renewal rate are assumptions rather than market evidence.
